fatal_errors: The proposed method is DFT-guided composition optimization, whereas the target method is experimental liquid-metal dealloying of directionally segregated WTaVTi in molten Cu.
It incorrectly proposes minimizing positive RHEA–Cu mixing enthalpy rather than exploiting selective Ti–Cu affinity and W/Ta/V–Cu immiscibility to replace Ti/V-rich channels with Cu.
It omits the essential 1200 °C, 96 h molten-Cu treatment and the directionally segregated precursor architecture required for millimeter-scale reaction and a stable bicontinuous microstructure.
The claimed interfacial energies, 20% reduction, temperature and pressure ranges, and falsification threshold are unsupported and appear fabricated.
It does not predict the retained RHEA ligament network, aligned Cu channels, or the W-rich passivating interlayer responsible for interface stability.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes only the broad challenge of combining RHEAs with Cu. It does not reconstruct the relevant solution: liquid-metal dealloying selectively removes Ti-rich interdendritic regions and replaces them with Cu, while immiscible refractory elements remain as continuous ligaments and a W-rich interlayer passivates the interface. Its DFT proposal is a generic computational screening strategy rather than a method demonstrated to produce large-scale reaction or the target stable architecture. The quantitative outcome and operating boundaries have no cited or supplied evidentiary basis. Although the proposed optimized-versus-unoptimized comparison is nominally testable, its measurements and thresholds are insufficiently defined and do not discriminate the actual selective-dealloying mechanism.
